What I do is whenever I see any of the senior posts I open my charting platform and go left to see and reconstruct why they took the trade. After a while you start seeing patterns and that is how you learn. And of course you can ask them after annotating your charts to see if you read it correctly but I believe after analysing senior members trades again and again you will start to see a pattern and the fog will clear away

Well, restart from the beginning.

I read a post from a MT with 5+ years experience in RTM (before it become RTM as we know it) and a beginner with 5- months experience that corrects his chart because it is different from the definition given in the past.

Well well. What I'm looking for? I'm looking for ITs activity. In other words, I'm looking for the levels where they controlled price (sure, because I don't think ITs are on the desk 24h/24... those are retailers. ITs are active only in some time of the day and when their away they puts tons of orders to defend some levels. When they back on the desk removes those levels and restart to play with hope and fear of retailers untils key levels for reversal are reached). In other words, I'm looking for places where their big orders lies. So, I'm not looking for nice places where plot red/blue rectangles.

Now, help me to understand where this is against RTM concepts

author: Ifmyante
text:
Many people study the recipes of great chefs.

Some do it so they can know every great recipe there is.

Others are simply looking for the best recipe, for them.

Long ago, before I had a complete understanding of the market, Mertch found something in what I was teaching which worked for him. He didn't need any more of what I taught after that. He had his method, his own understanding, which he then refined in his own kitchen.

He's not the first to do so, and he won't be the last, and that's one of the great beauties of this community!

Once your science is sound, you can begin to make your own art from it, and do things nobody else is doing.

If Mertch likes putting a sprig of coriander into his work, where I'd rather ginger, then yay for him, and yay for me too
